why: ChatGPT treated the question as a search for one product: it showed heated 12V 100Ah batteries side by side (Redodo $251.99, SOK $369, a premium smart model $629.99), and its only caveat was that some heaters need a minimum charging current (Power Queen specifies at least 10A), not that the shopper must buy a second item. The deciding facts are heater power and the heater's activation threshold, which a single-product comparison can cover, so the page should compare heated batteries and recommend one; the Redodo store could hold the battery plus a 14.6V charger, but nothing in the answer makes a charger part of the purchase.
